reading: Each green hollow box has a one-cell nub on one side. A reflected copy of the box (with its nub, clipped at the grid edge) is drawn on the opposite side, mirrored about the empty line just beyond that side. The copy is colour 1 when it goes left or right, and colour 8 when it goes up or down.

slots.subject: each 3-coloured object (box plus one-cell nub)
slots.axis: the row or column just past the box side opposite the nub
slots.colour: 1 for a horizontal reflection, 8 for a vertical one

why: every object gets exactly one mirror copy on the side away from its nub; the originals are unchanged

reading: The grid is split into large single-colour regions with scattered noise cells of one colour. The output is a 1x1 grid holding the colour of the region that contains the most noise cells.

slots.noise: the rarest colour, as single cells
slots.output: 1x1 grid of the colour of the region holding the most noise cells

why: the output colour's region holds strictly more noise cells than any other region

reading: There are hollow rectangles and scattered single cells of a few colours. The scattered cells are removed, and each rectangle's interior is filled with a checkerboard (starting at its top-left interior cell) in the scattered colour whose count equals the number of checkerboard cells.
verb: fill frames with checkerboard by count

slots.colour: the marker colour whose number of markers equals the checkerboard cell count of that interior
slots.pattern: checkerboard, starting with colour at the top-left interior cell
slots.markers: all isolated cells, cleared to background

why: the markers of each colour equal the checkerboard cells of exactly one frame; the frame outlines are unchanged

reading: Starting from the single 1 at the bottom-left, a diagonal of 1 is drawn upward, moving one column right per row and bouncing off the left and right edges. Every other cell becomes 8.

slots.source: the single 1 at the bottom-left corner
slots.path: one cell per row going up, x steps +1 and reverses at the grid's side borders

why: each row has exactly one 1, on the zigzag path; everything else is 8

reading: A 5-coloured L in the top-left corner frames a 3x3 template. The same 3x3 pattern occurs once elsewhere in the noisy grid, and a 5x5 outline of 5 is drawn around that occurrence.
verb: find template copy and outline it

slots.template: the 3x3 block at the top-left inside the 5 L
slots.match: the other 3x3 location with identical content
slots.mark: a one-cell 5 border around the match (5x5 ring)

why: the ring's interior equals the top-left template exactly; no other cell changes
invariants: all cells outside the drawn ring

reading: The grid is made of solid stripes (all rows, or all columns) with noise cells of other colours. Each stripe is cleaned to its majority colour: every row (or every column) becomes uniform.

slots.bands: each row if the stripes are horizontal, each column if vertical (the direction in which the majority line reproduces the output)
slots.colour: the majority colour of that row or column

why: every output row (or column) is uniform in the majority colour of the same input line

reading: A grey (5) column splits the grid into a left half and a right half. The output is the left half with the right half mirrored left-right and laid over it (non-zero cells merged).

slots.left: the panel left of the separator
slots.right: the panel right of it, flipped horizontally
slots.combine: overlay: a cell takes whichever side is non-background

why: output = left panel overlaid with the flipped right panel; the two never clash

reading: A region of 1 sits above a jagged 6 terrain. The column where the 1 region reaches deepest (the lowest valley) has its 1 cells turned to 9. The column with the highest 6 peak has the 1 cells above it turned to 4 (on a tie, the rightmost peak, i.e. the one farthest from the valley).

slots.valley: the column whose topmost 6 is lowest: its 1 cells become 9
slots.peak: the column whose topmost 6 is highest: its 1 cells become 4
slots.tie: unclear; the rightmost/farthest peak in train

why: only 1 cells in exactly two columns change; the 6 cells and the 0 top row are unchanged

reading: A small shape made of 2s sits in a noisy 0/5 grid. Copies of that shape in colour 2 are drawn at places where it fits entirely on 0 cells. Not every fitting place gets a copy (copies do not overlap, and the choice among the candidates is unclear).

slots.unit: the shape formed by the 2 cells
slots.anchors: placements where every cell of the shape is 0 (a non-overlapping subset; selection rule uncertain)

why: every added cell belongs to a complete copy of the 2 shape lying on former 0 cells; 5 cells never change

reading: Each green block is repeated diagonally downward in two directions, down-left and down-right. Each step moves by the block's own height down and its width sideways, until the copies leave the grid (clipped at the edges).
why: every added cell lies in a translated copy of an original block at an integer multiple of its diagonal step; the originals stay
